Team —

Forwarding Acuity's ask and my initial option set (see my note to Luke). Key points for approval:

- Deal: AH-3245, target 2-year prepaid with optional Year 3. Baseline annual prepay = $1.2M list year 1, ramp to $1.8M in year 2 per their forecast.
- Requested discount: target 30–35% on the prepaid baseline to secure the commit.
- Shelf: request for a ~15–20% prepaid buffer to cover Q1/Q4 peaks; Acuity wants reassignability or carry-forward for unused capacity.
- True-up cadence: quarterly.

Proposed Redwood structure for internal review:

A) Pricing bands: Year1 = 30% off list (on prepaid baseline), Year2 = 25% off list on annual prepay; if customer signs a 3rd year at month 18, Year3 = 20% off list.

B) Shelf buffer: up to 15% of prepaid baseline reserved for peak months, usable in Q1/Q4 only; excess peak usage billed at burst rates. Shelf is non-transferable to third parties but can be reassigned internally within Acuity with written notice (legal sign-off needed).

C) Carry-forward: allow carry-forward of up to 10% of unused baseline into the next quarter only; no indefinite accumulation. Alternatively, allow internal reassignment between Acuity business units with a 30-day notice and limits.

D) Approval ask: I can offer up to 30% discount without director approval. Anything deeper (<=35%) requires finance sign-off; >35% needs VP approval and will need a revenue-protection clause (true-up minimums or breakage uplift). Shelf buffer beyond 15% requires leadership sign-off.

Please review and reply with: (1) whether finance can approve up to 35% for this ACV profile with CPI escalator + quarterly true-up; (2) thoughts on shelf/carry-forward language that is acquirable by Legal. I'm attaching a draft pricing model.

Thanks — Marissa

Subject: Re: Fwd: Multi-year prepaid ask + shelf capacity for Acuity — pricing approval request

Marissa —

Thanks for the summary. Quick takes:

- Finance: we can approve up to 35% on year-1 prepaid provided there is a 12-month minimum revenue guarantee and a quarterly true-up that can hit minimum ARR thresholds. We want to avoid long carry-forward windows; agree with 10% into the subsequent quarter only.

- Shelf: 15% buffer is reasonable for Q1/Q4, but make the buffer explicitly timeboxed (Q1 start/end + Q4 start/end) and subject to maximum quarterly consumption at X2 baseline rate before bursting to on-demand. No indefinite reassignment to unrelated third parties; internal reassignment OK with an audit trail.

- Legal: will need to approve the reassignment language — suggest we mark it as "internal transferability subject to Redwood audit and 30-day notice".

- Discount clawback: include a 10% clawback on realized savings if true-ups show usage < 70% of committed baseline across year 1 (protects revenue if they underconsume).

If you keep the 30% baseline and present the 35% as conditional (Finance-approved if GUARNTEE terms met), that gives us negotiating room.

Happy to sync quickly with you before sending to Acuity.

Kimberly Park
Director, Sales Operations
Redwood Inference
